key_insight: SoftServe is a scalable quasi-Newton framework that keeps curvature estimates positive definite by construction, enabling deep-learning optimization without line searches or manual curvature fixes.
engineering_relevance: It offers a GPU-friendly path to faster, more stable training on large, ill-conditioned neural networks by replacing expensive matrix decompositions with coupled Newton-Schulz iterations.
method: Builds curvature from a variational objective even when negative curvature is present
Provides diagonal and Kronecker-factored variants that remain positive definite
Uses stable coupled Newton-Schulz iterations for matrix operations on GPUs
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong results on ill-conditioned benchmarks including recurrent networks, deep autoencoders, physics-informed neural networks, and a 136M-parameter diffusion model, often outperforming Adam, Muon, and SOAP.
watch_item: Performance depends on iterative matrix approximations, so numerical stability, iteration count, and memory/compute cost should be validated for each model and hardware setting.
paper_title: SoftServe: A Scalable Quasi-Newton Method for Deep Learning
